title: U.S. Department of State — Liberia health data systems under the America First Global Health Strategy MOU, 2025
description:
"2.5.3 Funding Plan: The U.S. Government intends to provide the following amount of funding for data systems in each of the specified years, subject to the availability of funds: 2026 $8,056,796; 2027 $6,705,396; 2028 $6,517,396; 2029 $2,054,096; 2030 $2,800,000." In 2026 this includes "$1,654,099 for mSupply, $827,050 for EMR, $1,620,287 for LIS, $620,287 for eIDSR/IDSR and $413,525 for HMIS/DHIS2"; over the term, "$2,676,744 for Electronic Medical Records systems, $2,007,558 for lab information system, $2,007,558 for eIDSR/IDSR $1,338,372 for HMIS/DHIS2 at its national health data warehouse."

The sum is one line of a wider MOU whose total planned US support is US$124,418,400 against Liberia's US$50,725,704 (Appendix 1). It is non-binding: "This MOU is not an international agreement and does not give rise to legal rights and obligations" (6.9), and every figure is "subject to the availability of funds".
recipient_organisation: Government of Liberia / Ministry of Health

title: World Bank — Liberia GREAT digital-ID and digital-government, 2025
description: "Liberia's Ministry of Finance and Development Planning launched the Governance Reform Accountability Transformation (GREAT) project on 20 March 2025 in Monrovia. Funded by the World Bank's ID Credit Program with $30 million (plus an additional $13m for digital infrastructure), GREAT seeks to enroll at least 2 million Liberians for the national digital ID through the NIR." Running to November 2030, it also builds a digital-government ecosystem beginning with nine institutions.
recipient_organisation: GREAT project / Ministry of Finance and Development Planning

title: Orange Telecom Project in Liberia \u2013 Expansion Guarantee
description: MIGA guarantee of $81 million to Orange Cote d'Ivoire Participations (OCIP) covering existing equity investment and future retained earnings for telecom operations and expansion in Orange Liberia Inc., including construction of telecom towers, installation of fiber optic cable, and provision of telecom services and mobile finance services. Risks: Expropriation and War and Civil Disturbance for up to 8 years. Issued September 8, 2023 (FY2024). MIGA's first contract in Liberia since 2016.

title: World Bank — Liberia REALISE Informal Sector Employment Recovery Project, 2021
description: "The objective is to increase access to income earning opportunities for the vulnerable in the informal sector in response to the COVID-19 crisis in Liberia." (original PDO, approved 12-Mar-2021). Current PDO, approved as part of an additional-financing package on 22-Dec-2022: "To increase access to income-earning opportunities for the vulnerable in the informal sector in response to crises, expand income and livelihood support to poor and food insecure households, and improve efficiency in managing social protection programs in Liberia."

title: Escotel Liberia \u2013 Solar Power for Telecom Towers Guarantee
description: MIGA political risk guarantee of $12.06 million to Escotel Mauritius covering its investment in Escotel Liberia Inc., which installs and operates solar-hybrid power systems at ~612 telecom tower sites in Liberia owned/operated by Orange Liberia. Avoids 158,000 tCO2e over the guarantee period. Risks: Transfer Restriction, Expropriation, War and Civil Disturbance for up to 10 years.
